Four call sites in the REST module (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest`) call `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet`. I found them with a single regex search for `saveOrderSet(` and read the surrounding code in two of the files. I did not search the other modules, such as `omod-1.8` and `omod-common`, for other users of `OrderSetService`, so there could be more.

- **`OrderSetResource1_12.save`** (line 71) calls `saveOrderSet(orderSet)` and returns the result. This is the main path for creating and updating order sets over `/ws/rest/v1/orderset`. Just before the call, it replaces each member's concept and order type with the persisted objects looked up by UUID.
- **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.save`** (line 166) adds the new member to its parent order set, then saves the parent.
- **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.delete`** (line 154) retires the member on its parent order set, then saves the parent.
- **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.purge`** (line 174) removes the member from its parent order set, then saves the parent.

A test also calls the method directly: `OrderSetMemberController1_12Test`, line 85 (`omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_12/`). It uses it to set up a test order set, so it could fail if the behaviour changed.
